cards.question: What does the `revenue_model/` work in google-sheets-api-python build in HubSpot for the 20 manual-input revenue lines?
cards.answer: A HubSpot custom object `revenue_plan_line`: one record per line, bound to its canonical Company where a binding exists.
cards.explanation: The repository is a fork of a Google Sheets API tutorial; the owner's own work is `revenue_model/`: a design document, the S0-S9 runbook, the schema payload and three scripts. Before it, the 20 lines existed only as sheet rows with no CRM identity and no company relationship.
cards.anchor: Twenty loose sticky notes peel off a spreadsheet; each lands on an index card of its own, tied by one string to a company's doorplate.
cards.example: curl -X POST https://api.hubapi.com/crm-object-schemas/v3/schemas -H "Authorization: Bearer $HUBSPOT_PRIVATE_APP_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @revenue_model/schema_revenue_plan_line.json  # creates the object (S2)
cards.evidence_quote: One new custom object: `revenue_plan_line` (label "Revenue Plan Line"), one record per model line item (20 records)

cards.question: Which system-of-record split does google-sheets-api-python's making layer rest on?
cards.answer: HubSpot owns a line's identity and company link; the Sheet owns its values, mirrored Sheet -> CRM ONE way.
cards.explanation: Planners edit the Sheet, never the mirror; the upsert is the only writer of `amount_*` and re-running it reconciles the copy. Breaks if undone: values drift silently between the CRM mirror and the Sheet (DFMEA RPN 175). see 70
cards.anchor: Planners write on a whiteboard and a camera copies it to the lobby screen; scribbling on the lobby screen changes nothing upstream and is wiped at the next copy.
cards.confusables: two-way sync — values would be editable on BOTH sides; here the CRM copy is read-only by rule and overwritten by the next upsert.
cards.evidence_quote: system of record for values = Sheet; for identity/relationship = CRM

cards.question: google-sheets-api-python: a plan line has one value per year. How many `revenue_plan_line` records does it get, and where do the years live?
cards.answer: ONE record per line item (20 in all); its years are six number properties `amount_2025`..`amount_2030` in $M.
cards.explanation: Rejected: one record per line x year (120 records), which would flood a company sidebar with year-records and multiply association upkeep by six. Cost accepted: adding a year is a schema change, done once a year.
cards.confusables: `li_values.csv` row — the CSV is LONG (one row per line x year, 120 rows); the CRM record is WIDE (one per line, six amount properties).
cards.evidence_quote: 1 record = 1 model line** (not 1 per line×year, not 1 per pursuit)

cards.question: google-sheets-api-python · `crm_associate_companies.py`: complete the two `company_binding_mode` values whose lines get a company edge.
cards.cloze: `bindable_lines()` keeps a catalog row only when its `company_binding_mode` is {{c1::VERIFIED}} or {{c1::VERIFIED_WITH_DUPES}} and its company id is not empty.
cards.explanation: This is the governance gate in code: a line whose account is not pinned to one canonical record stays unassociated rather than wrongly associated. With the committed catalog it keeps 15 lines and skips 5.
cards.confusables: `PROSPECTIVE` / `AGGREGATE` — valid enum values too, but SKIPPED: those lines stay unassociated by design.

cards.question: google-sheets-api-python · WORKFLOW runbook: recite the 6 steps S0 to S5, from preflight to verified company associations.
steps: S0 preflight -> Enterprise tier, a free custom-object slot and a token confirmed
S1 dedup -> duplicate company records merged INTO the canonical record (irreversible)
S3 create the `Plan line` association label -> edges to companies can carry the name
cards.answer: preflight · dedup · schema · label · upsert · associate + verify
cards.explanation: The order is by dependency and each step has a Verify gate. The load-bearing constraint: S5 runs strictly after S1 and S4, so every edge lands on a canonical company that still exists and on a record that is already loaded. S6-S9 (permissions, Sheet re-sync, acceptance, DFMEA re-score) follow.
cards.anchor: A registry clerk checks her licence, glues twin company folders into one, prints a blank form, inks a stamp, fills 20 forms, then staples 15 of them to folders and recounts.
cards.evidence_quote: Runs strictly **after S1 (dedup) and S4 (records exist)**

cards.question: Which script in google-sheets-api-python loads the 20 plan-line records into HubSpot (runbook step S4)?
cards.explanation: `--dry-run` prints the count and the first input and returns BEFORE the token is read; `--execute` POSTs slices of 100 inputs to the batch upsert endpoint. Exactly one of the two flags is required. Records ONLY, no associations.
cards.example: python revenue_model/crm_upsert_plan_lines.py --object-type <fullyQualifiedName> --dry-run  # '20 records to upsert into ...' then the first input as JSON
cards.confusables: `crm_associate_companies.py` — same flags plus `--verify`, but it creates EDGES to companies, never records.

cards.question: google-sheets-api-python · `build_inputs`: predict the exact value of the expression on the last line of the snippet below.
cards.code_snippet:
# li_catalog.csv, first row: li_cat_new_sealsq_prospects
# li_values.csv: li_cat_new_sealsq_prospects,11,...,2026,0.2,...
for row in csv.DictReader(f):
    values.setdefault(row["li_key"], {})[int(row["year"])] = row["value_musd"]
# ...
for y in YEARS:
    props[f"amount_{y}"] = values[c["li_key"]].get(y, "0")
inputs.append({"idProperty": "li_key", "id": c["li_key"], "properties": props})
# ...
build_inputs()[0]["properties"]["amount_2026"]
cards.answer: `'0.2'` — a STRING: `csv.DictReader` yields text and `build_inputs()` forwards `value_musd` verbatim, pivoting one CSV row per year into one `amount_<year>` property.
cards.explanation: (1) The 2026 row of the first catalog line holds `0.2`. (2) It is stored as text under the int key 2026. (3) `.get(y, "0")` returns that text; only a MISSING year falls back to `"0"`. No float conversion happens anywhere, so the model's figures reach the API exactly as typed.
cards.evidence_quote: li_cat_new_sealsq_prospects,11,Catalog Product Customers,New SEALSQ Prospects,2026,0.2,Line item manual input,None

cards.question: Why does google-sheets-api-python model plan lines as a custom object `revenue_plan_line` rather than as HubSpot native line items?
cards.answer: Native line items have NO association type to companies: they hang only on deals, quotes and other commerce objects, with a single parent, and are cascade-deleted with it.
cards.explanation: The plan lines must hang on Companies and outlive any deal. Breaks if undone: every line needs a parent deal, enters deal analytics and vanishes when that deal is deleted. The products catalog was ruled out too: products cannot be associated with other objects. see 61
cards.anchor: A price tag sewn into one coat: sell or burn the coat and the tag goes with it, and nobody can pin that tag onto the customer's own file.
cards.confusables: native `line_items` — a child of ONE deal or quote with no company edge; the custom object is a standalone record whose only edge IS the company.

cards.question: Why does google-sheets-api-python's `revenue_plan_line` schema list `COMPANY` as its ONLY associated object rather than also linking plan lines to deals?
cards.answer: With NO join path to deals, plan values cannot leak into pipelines, forecast tools or win-rate reports: isolation rule R1 makes R3 structural instead of a matter of discipline.
cards.explanation: It is the reason a second 'planning' deal pipeline was rejected: deals always feed forecast analytics. The S2 gate checks that COMPANY is the only entry. Breaks if undone: planning figures get counted as live sales pipeline.
cards.anchor: A planner's wish list kept in a room with one door, opening onto the company shelves; the sales scoreboard hangs in another building with no corridor between them.
cards.confusables: a 'planning' deal pipeline — the lines would BE deals and appear in forecasts; the custom object has no deal edge at all.
cards.evidence_quote: Prevents any join path that could leak plan values into sales analytics.

cards.question: google-sheets-api-python: what does isolation rule R5 demand of every dollar in the revenue model?
cards.answer: It enters through exactly ONE feed: a pursuit covered by a plan line is excluded from the weighted-pipe scope.
cards.explanation: It answers the top DFMEA risk, double counting (RPN 216 = 9 x 6 x 4). R4 keeps the deal weighted-pipe layer (`weighted_amount_calculated`, cf. [private project]) read-only, and that pipe feeds only the Catalog segment line. The audit is quarterly and manual: no script exists for it.
cards.confusables: R1 — R1 forbids any EDGE from the object to deals; R5 forbids the same MONEY arriving twice, even when no edge exists.
cards.evidence_quote: every dollar enters the model through exactly one feed

cards.question: google-sheets-api-python: which property makes re-running the plan-line upsert safe?
cards.answer: `li_key`: unique-value text sent as `idProperty`, so each run is create-or-update with no record-id bookkeeping.
cards.explanation: No plan-line record id is stored anywhere in the repository (the ids in `li_catalog.csv` are COMPANY ids); the key is also the join column between the CRM record, `LI_CATALOG` and `LI_VALUES`. The association script resolves record ids from it at run time. The schema marks it `hasUniqueValue` and says never to rename it.
cards.anchor: A cloakroom ticket: hand in the same number twice and the attendant walks to the same hook; a second coat never appears.
cards.confusables: `label` — the display name, which may change FREELY; the key never does.

cards.question: What makes google-sheets-api-python's `deploy_line_items.py` able to write to a Google Sheet?
cards.answer: The fork's `pygs.Pygs` wrapper, which authenticates with a service-account key JSON at the repository root. In this fork that file is a PLACEHOLDER: put a real key there and share the spreadsheet with the service account as editor.
cards.explanation: `pygs.py` builds its credentials at IMPORT time, so the deploy script imports `Pygs` inside `main()` rather than at module level. Until the key is real, the Sheet re-sync (S7) cannot run.
cards.example: python revenue_model/deploy_line_items.py <spreadsheet_id>  # clears and rewrites LI_CATALOG and LI_VALUES, appends the checksum block
cards.confusables: the HubSpot side — the two CRM scripts need only the env var `HUBSPOT_PRIVATE_APP_TOKEN` and the standard library; ONLY the Sheet deploy needs the key file and the Google packages.
cards.evidence_quote: from pygs import Pygs # imported late: module-level auth needs a real key file

cards.question: google-sheets-api-python: which command proves the line-to-company associations are right, and what is its passing sign?
cards.answer: `python revenue_model/crm_associate_companies.py --object-type <fullyQualifiedName> --verify` — last line `verify: 15/15 correct; expected total = 15`, exit code 0.
cards.explanation: A line is OK only when its associated companies equal EXACTLY the one canonical id, so a leftover second edge is a MISMATCH and the exit code is 1. The repository has no test suite: this gate and the Sheet checksum block are the proofs.
cards.example: python revenue_model/crm_associate_companies.py --object-type <fullyQualifiedName> --verify; echo $?  # 0 only when every bindable line matches

cards.question: google-sheets-api-python: `li_catalog.csv` vs the deployed `LI_CATALOG` Sheet tab: what is the ONE difference?
cards.answer: `li_catalog.csv` in the repository is the source of truth and holds the canonical company ids; the deployed `LI_CATALOG` tab is a STALE copy, published before the canonical designation.
cards.explanation: All three scripts read the CSV, never the tab. Fix: `python revenue_model/deploy_line_items.py <spreadsheet_id>` (S7) clears the tab and rewrites it from the CSV.
cards.anchor: A master ledger locked in the office and a photocopy pinned in the corridor weeks ago: corrections go into the ledger while the corridor copy keeps last month's entries.
cards.confusables: `LI_CATALOG` tab — shows the pre-canonical binding modes until S7 is re-run; reading it instead of the CSV gives the WRONG association targets.
cards.evidence_quote: `li_catalog.csv` in this repo is the source of truth.

cards.question: google-sheets-api-python: you retire a plan line by setting `active=false` in HubSpot, as the design prescribes, and leave its row in `li_catalog.csv`. What does the next `crm_upsert_plan_lines.py --execute` do to it, and what is the smallest fix?
cards.answer: It UN-RETIRES the line. (1) `build_inputs()` hard-codes `"active": "true"` for every catalog row. (2) `li_catalog.csv` has NO `active` column, so no row can say otherwise. (3) Smallest fix: add an `active` column to the catalog and read it in `build_inputs()`; until then, remove the row from the catalog before retiring the record.
cards.explanation: Drift between design and code: the design says retirement is `active=false`, never delete; the code resets the flag on every run. Inputs are built ONLY from catalog rows, so a record whose row was removed is left untouched by the upsert.

cards.question: What is the next planned step for google-sheets-api-python's revenue_model, the one designed phase that has no code yet?
cards.answer: The Phase D export — DESIGN TARGET: search the `active=true` records, batch-read their company associations, write `LI_VALUES` staging and compare checksums. It is the detector for Sheet/CRM drift.
cards.explanation: The CRM search API does not return associations, so the export needs a SECOND call or it silently drops the line-to-company mapping. `revenue_model/` holds three scripts (upsert, associate, Sheet deploy) and none for the export.
cards.evidence_quote: checksum against the sheet block; alert on mismatch (detects drift, risk #2)
